Half a minute in every five while you wear your watch. Off saves battery.

Most of a night is light sleep. Deep sleep comes mostly early in the night, REM mostly towards morning. Your watch estimates this from heart rate and movement, not a sleep lab. Slide over the chart to see a moment.
Mostly how long you slept: 7 to 9 hours counts in full. Then how calm the night was: the first 10 minutes awake cost nothing. Deep sleep and REM count least, because a wrist can tell them least well.
The lowest heart rate of the night. It says most next to your own usual: a cold or a drink can push it up for a night or two. Not a diagnosis.
From your last nights, at most 14. Give or take says how far a usual night is from that time: the smaller, the steadier.
A minute counts when you walk briskly, about 100 steps a minute. Health advice for adults is 150 minutes a week.
If you lie still for 20 minutes during the day, your watch asks whether you slept. Only a yes makes it a nap. You can also start one yourself on your watch.
Half a minute of measuring every five minutes while you wear your watch. A gap means it was off your wrist or could not measure.

Five minutes before your alarm your watch starts one long, quiet buzz that rises and falls a few times, a little more each time. It never gets strong: your alarm wakes you the rest of the way. Works during a sleep recording.
